issue: IF-07 makes PWR_KILL_N active-low, but its candidate pin is GPIO0_A4 = PMIC_PWR_CTRL_M0 (pin 63), whose reset default is a pull-down ([DS] Table 2-1 p.19: 'PMIC_PWR_CTRL_M0/PWM1_M0/GPIO0_A4_d'). From the button press until Linux's gpio-poweroff takes the pin (BootROM, SPL, U-Boot, kernel: several seconds), KILL sits low and is asserted. It is also 0 V before VCC_3V3 comes up, so any pull-up to 3.3 V does not help. A controller of the LTC2954 type would cut VCC5V0_SYS once its turn-on blanking ends, so the board would never finish booting.
fix: In architecture.md IF-07 and D-03, add the rule that the kill line is inactive at 0 V and while the SoC pin is in its reset state. Option (a): make the kill active-high (net PWR_KILL) on a pin that defaults to pull-down, such as GPIO0_A4_d. If the chosen controller's KILL input is active-low, put an N-MOSFET inverter between them, with gate pull-down and drain pull-up to the controller's own always-on supply. Option (b): keep it active-low, but only with a pin that defaults to pull-up plus an external pull-up to an always-on rail, and confirm the controller's KILL blanking time covers the 3.3 V ramp. Record the choice in decisions.md. Phase 2 must check the pin's reset pull, and Phase 3 the controller's KILL timing.

issue: IF-13/IF-22 say USB_SEL defaults by resistor to USB-C and that USBA_VBUS_EN starts off. They do not require the chosen SoC pins' reset pulls (_u/_d, about 50 kΩ internal) to agree with those external defaults. A pin whose internal pull disagrees with a weak external resistor could leave the mux on USB-A or VBUS_USBA on during BootROM/MASKROM, which breaks USB flashing.
fix: Add to architecture.md §4/§5: USB_SEL and USBA_VBUS_EN must sit on pins whose reset pull matches the safe state (USB-C selected, VBUS_USBA off). Otherwise the external resistor must be 10 kΩ or less so it wins. Carry this into the Phase 2 pinmap checks.

issue: On [LF], U6 (VCC_3V3) EN = PWR_EN, which reaches the header pin '3V3_En' through R24 0R. The only pull-up to VCC5V0_SYS is R41, marked '1K/NC' (it may not be fitted). The architecture says 'U6 EN is on PWR_EN through R43 200 kΩ' but never says what drives PWR_EN high in our design. If this is copied with R41 not fitted and no header drive, VCC_3V3 never comes up and the board will not boot.
fix: In architecture.md §3, note that PWR_EN must be pulled up to VCC5V0_SYS (R41 fitted, 1 kΩ per [LF]) or driven from the onoff block. Mark it as an open item for TP-D3 sequencing.

issue: Interface names in the diagram do not match the IF table. The diagram says 'USB_C_DP/DM' where IF-21 says USBC_DP/DM. The arrow soc→usb carries USBA_VBUS_EN, but IF-13 routes it to the switch in pmu. prot's ESD on the USB-C/USB-A data lines has no arrow or IF row. VCC_3V3→usb mux, VCC_3V3→PWR LED (IF-29) and VCC_1V8→ui (RECOVERY pull-up) are in the IF table but not drawn. The claim 'every arrow has an IF row' holds, but some IF rows have no arrow.
fix: Use one net name (USBC_DP/DM), draw the USBA_VBUS_EN arrow from soc to usbsw, and add an ESD arrow (prot↔usbc/usb data lines) with its own IF row. Draw the VCC_3V3→usb/ui and VCC_1V8→ui power arrows, or state that the IF table is the authoritative list.

issue: D-09 says [LF] only drives an LED from the 1.8 V-only GPIO3_C6, but [LF] also has the net LED_GREEN on pin 62 (GPIO0_A3_u, PMU domain at 3.3 V). Pins 74/77/78 carry AVS_ARM, LED_PWM_IR and LED_PWM_WHITE. A copy-first status LED pin is being missed.

issue: §5 says 'boots from microSD during bring-up, then from SPI NAND', but neither the BootROM's media order (SD vs FSPI) nor how to force SD boot once the NAND is programmed is cited. I could not confirm it either: [DS] §1.2.2 only lists the devices.

issue: D-03's candidate controllers (LTC2954/LTC2955, MAX16150, STM6601) are all unverified for a ≥8 s hard-off, and are likely Extended or low-stock parts at LCSC. R4 has no fallback if none of them qualifies.

issue: D-16 and architecture.md §4.1 use an internal pull of 'about 50 kΩ (UNVERIFIED)' and say that if a pin's reset pull disagrees with the safe state, an external resistor of ≤10 kΩ wins. [DS] Table 3-3 p.21 actually gives Rpu/Rpd = 16 / 25 / 43 kΩ (min/typ/max). Worst case is a 16 kΩ internal pull-up at 3.465 V against a 10 kΩ external pull-down. The node then sits at 3.465×10/26 = 1.33 V, above the 0.8 V Vil and inside the undefined band of typical mux SEL and load-switch EN inputs. A disagreeing pin chosen under this rule could therefore leave USB_SEL on the USB-A side (MASKROM over USB-C breaks) or turn USBA_VBUS_EN on during BootROM.
fix: In D-16 and §4.1, replace 'about 50 kΩ' with '16–43 kΩ, [DS] Table 3-3 p.21' and drop the UNVERIFIED tag. Change the rule to: use only pins whose reset pull matches the safe state (preferred). If that is impossible, the external resistor must be ≤ 2.0 kΩ (16 kΩ×0.4 V/(3.465−0.4) V = 2.09 kΩ). Phase 2 must check the resulting voltage against the receiving IC's VIL/VIH.

issue: PWR_KILL sits on GPIO0_A4. Its function 1 is pmic_sleep_m0: group pmicm0_pins in the Luckfox SDK's rv1106-pinctrl.dtsi (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LuckfoxTECH/luckfox-pico/main/sysdrv/source/kernel/arch/arm/boot/dts/rv1106-pinctrl.dtsi), and [DS] Table 2-1 p.19 names it PMIC_PWR_CTRL_M0. If the DTS or the PMU sleep configuration ever muxes this pin to PMIC sleep, the PMU drives it during system suspend. That would assert the kill and switch the board off instead of suspending. GPIO0_A3 (the status LED pin) is pmic_sleep_m1 and has the same issue.
fix: Add to D-03 and §4.1: pin 63 must stay in GPIO mode at all times. Phase 2 pinmap records the iomux. The Phase 8 DTS must not reference pmicm0_pins/pmicm1_pins and must not enable PMIC-sleep output in the PMU sleep configuration (or suspend is disabled). An alternative is to pick another `_d` GPIO in a 3.3 V domain that has no PMU function.

issue: D-09, IF-28 and R7.5 say the status LED 'copies [LF]'s LED_GREEN on pin 62'. In [LF] the text LED_GREEN appears only once, as a net label at U1 pin 62 (x≈359,y≈202). The sheet has exactly one LED part (COLED1 = LED1, through R56 on GPIO3_C6, pin 4). So LED_GREEN is an unconnected stub and the LED circuit is not copied from a proven design. GPIO0_A3 also resets with a pull-up (`_u`), so an active-high LED would glow during reset.
fix: Reword D-09, IF-28 and R7.5: 'pin choice reuses the [LF] net name; the LED circuit itself is a deviation (only LED1 on GPIO3_C6 exists in [LF])'. Fix the polarity now: anode to VCC_3V3 through a resistor, cathode to pin 62 (active-low). The reset pull-up then keeps the LED dark until Linux drives the pin low.

issue: USB_VBUSDET (IF-23) is fed from the USB-C VBUS, which is also the board's only power input. It is therefore always high while the board runs, whatever is attached. [DS] Table 2-1 lists no USB_ID pin. Hardware cannot tell host from device role, and when USB_SEL selects USB-A, the controller still sees VBUS present. The architecture does not say how the controller role follows USB_SEL.
fix: Add a note to D-05, IF-23 and §5: the USB role is set by software in step with USB_SEL (dr_mode/usb-role-switch plan for Phase 8). Have Phase 2 research whether RV1106 host mode needs VBUSDET low. If it does, add a gate that forces VBUSDET low while USB-A is selected (mark UNVERIFIED until then). MASKROM is unaffected, because [LF] has the same always-high VBUSDET.

issue: Architecture §3 summarises '3.3 V rails 3.0–3.3–3.465 V (ETH_AVDD3V3 2.97–3.63 V)' and '1.8 V analog rails 1.62–1.8–1.98 V'. [DS] Table 3-2 p.20 actually gives USB_AVDD3V3 3.0–3.6 V, RTC_AVDD3V3 1.6–3.6 V, OSC_AVDD1V8/PLL_AVDD1V8 max = TBD and DDR_PLL_AVDD1V8 min/max = TBD. The summary is conservative but does not match the cited table.

issue: The eth block lists the jack, ETH_EXTR, the 0 Ω links and Bob-Smith termination, but not how the transformer centre taps connect. In [LF] J2, CT pins 4 and 5 each go to GND through C66/C67 '103/10V' (10 nF), with no bias supply. The shield/pin 8 goes through C68 '0R/1nF/100V' and a 1nF/2KV. If this is not recorded, a later phase could tie CT to 3.3 V, as current-mode PHYs require.
fix: Add to the eth row in architecture.md §1: 'CT pins to GND via 10 nF each (copy [LF] C66/C67 103/10V), no CT bias (voltage-mode embedded PHY); shield via C68 0R/1nF/100V option'. Cite the [LF] 'Ethernet' block J2.

issue: Pin 25 USB_VBUSDET (row 25 of pinmap.csv, architecture IF-23) gets its 10k/18k divider (Luckfox R2/R5) from the raw USB-C VBUS. On this board the onoff switch (D-03) keeps VCC5V0_SYS, and so every SoC rail, off while the cable is still plugged in. The result is about 3.2 V through 10 kΩ into a pin of an unpowered SoC, which can back-power VCC_3V3/USB_AVDD3V3 through the ESD diodes. That can stop the SoC from starting cleanly from off, and it is a reliability risk. Luckfox avoids this only because its SoC is always powered whenever VBUS is present; its schematic has the note 'USB power must supply always' next to USB_VBUSDET. Separately, the pinmap's domain cite 'Table 3-7 USB levels' does not specify VBUSDET at all.
fix: Feed the R2/R5 divider from the switched VCC5V0_SYS instead of VBUS_5V. USB-C is the only power input, so VBUSDET still reads high whenever the SoC is on, and MASKROM and gadget mode are unaffected. Alternatively, gate the divider with the onoff output. Update pinmap.csv row 25 (external, source), architecture.md IF-23 and usbc/power-tree text, and add a new decision D-27. Replace the 'Table 3-7' cite with '[LF] R2/R5; VBUSDET input threshold/max UNVERIFIED in [DS]'. Add a check for this pin to check_pinmap.py.

issue: The header I2C lines have no external pull-ups specified: pins 85/86 (I2C3_M1, header 5/3) and 104/105 (I2C1_M1, header 28/27). The `external` column lists only the header pin. Pins 85, 86 and 104 have internal reset pull-downs, and Pi-style accessories expect pull-ups on the board (header 3/5).

issue: The debug UART RX (pin 80) connects straight to the 3-pin header. A USB-UART adapter left attached while the board is off, which is now a normal state because of the onoff button, holds its TX at 3.3 V and back-powers the unpowered VCCIO1 domain through pin 80.

issue: The check_pinmap.py checks are weaker than they look. C9 checks the pinmap's own reset_pull column instead of deriving the pull from the datasheet suffix. C4 uses a substring match with a special-case hack for 'SDMMC_D0'. C7 has no check for pins that are driven while their domain is unpowered (the problem behind the major finding). I checked the reset pulls independently and found no mismatch, so this is a robustness issue, not a wrong result.

issue: architecture.md is out of date for the debug UART. The `uart` block row and the IF-24 row (UART2_TX/RX) do not mention the D-30 1k series resistors or that TP9/TP10 sit on the SoC side. Line 189 still says the console baud rate is the Rockchip default 1 500 000 (UNVERIFIED). D-15 and research.md (from SDK rv1106.dtsi lines 227-230) say the fiq-debugger console is 115200.

issue: D-27, research.md §3 and pinmap row 25 say the VBUS-detect pin (25) never sees voltage while the SoC is unpowered. That is too strong. At power-up, the switched 5 V rail and the divider's ~3.2 V appear before the 3.3 V and 1.8 V USB supplies finish ramping. The 3.3 V buck enable goes through R43 200k plus an RC, so this lasts milliseconds. Luckfox behaves the same way, so the design is acceptable, but the claim is inaccurate.

issue: The truncation incident shows pinmap.csv is hand-edited after it is generated and has no backup. The generator and the round-2 patch script exist only in the scratchpad (`p2/gen_pinmap.py`, `p2/apply_r2.py`). I found no lost content: all 129 rows agree with the datasheet, the Luckfox schematic and decisions D-19 to D-31. Even so, the file cannot be reproduced from the project folder.

issue: The notes on pinmap rows 105 (GPIO2_B0) and 110 (GPIO2_A1) cite a 'worst-case 16k internal reset pull-down'. The datasheet prints no _u/_d/_z suffix for these two pins, so their reset pull comes only from the Luckfox symbol and is not confirmed in the datasheet. This is harmless, because the external pull-up or a header input decides the level either way.

issue: The output filters on U4 (VDD_0V9) and U7 (VCC_DDR) do not match any combination TI lists as proven. TLV62569 datasheet SLVSDG1C p.9 Table 4: for 0.6–1.2 V with 2.2 µH, only 2×22 µF is checked; for 1.2–1.8 V with 2.2 µH, only 22 µF or 2×22 µF. The design uses U4 = 2.2 µH + 22 µF + 4.7 µF and U7 = 2.2 µH + 10 µF. The executor also replaced the Luckfox inductors (1.0 µH on L2 and L4), so these filters match neither TI's table nor the Luckfox board. power.md §2 says they are 'inside the [TLV] Table 4 proven combinations', which is false. An unstable core or DDR rail would stop the board from booting.
fix: Change U4 to 2.2 µH + 2×22 µF + 100 nF and U7 to 2.2 µH + 22 µF + 100 nF; both are TI's recommended '++' combinations. Keep 6.8 pF feed-forward with the 100 kΩ bottom resistor. Correct the power.md §2 sentence and D-32, and add a check_power.py test that looks up each buck's L/C pair in Table 4.

issue: The main P-MOSFET (Q_PWR, AO3401A) turns on for a few milliseconds every time the cable is plugged in. Its soft-start capacitor C_GD (33 nF, gate to drain) is much larger than the FET's own gate capacitance (about 0.65 nF, AO3401A p.2), and the gate pull-up R_GS is a weak 100 kΩ. When VBUS steps up, C_GD holds the gate near the drain (0 V), so the gate-source voltage is about −4.9 V and the FET is fully on. VCC5V0_SYS then jumps to about 4 V for several ms with no button press. U4 (enable tied to VCC5V0_SYS) and possibly U5/U7 start, so rails come up partly and out of order. Hot-plug ringing on the 2.2 µF input also reaches the bucks, whose input abs-max is 6 V (TLV62569 p.3). This contradicts power.md §6.2, which says the board stays off after plug-in until the button is pressed.
fix: Remove C_GD, or add a gate-to-source capacitor C_GS of at least 10 × C_GD so the plug-in coupling stays below the 0.5 V minimum gate threshold. Example: C_GD 3.3 nF and C_GS 47 nF, with R_G re-sized to get the wanted ramp. Recompute the inrush current and the turn-off time. Add a plug-in case to power.md §6 showing VGS stays above −0.5 V while VBUS ramps in 10 µs to 1 ms.

issue: The sequencing proof (power.md §3 and check_power.py P7) uses 0.85 V as the lowest voltage at which a regulator's enable pin can switch on. TLV62569 p.4 lists VIL as min 0.4 V and typ 0.85 V, and VIH only as typ 0.95 V and max 1.2 V. So 0.85 V is a typical value; the datasheet only guarantees a switch point between 0.4 V and 1.2 V. With 0.4 V, U6 (3.3 V) can enable at 44 ms × ln(5.25/4.85) ≈ 3.5 ms, while U5/U7 (1.8 V and DDR) may enable as late as 5.8 ms. 'VCC_3V3 and nPOR last' is therefore not guaranteed. nPOR follows VCC_3V3 through a 10 µs RC (R12 1 kΩ, C38 10 nF), so reset can release before VCC_1V8 (oscillator/PLL) and VCC_DDR are up. That puts first boot at risk. The Luckfox hand notes ('200K->100K' at R14, '100K->200K' at R43) also show that Luckfox deliberately made 1.8 V and DDR start before 3.3 V.
fix: Make the order independent of RC timing: feed U6's enable network (R41 → PWR_EN → R43/C65) from VCC_1V8 instead of VCC5V0_SYS. VCC_1V8 is at least 1.74 V, above VIH max 1.2 V, and well under the 6 V EN abs-max. Re-size R43/C65 so 3.3 V is still up long before the 400 ms KILL blanking ends. Alternatively, use TLV62569P parts and chain their power-good outputs. Rewrite P7 to use the 0.4–1.2 V threshold window, and re-check that U4 is good (≤ 1.2 ms) before U5/U7 can enable (≥ 1.59 ms at 0.4 V).

issue: The VCC_3V3 divider (45.3k/10k) gives 3.318 V nominal and up to 3.440 V worst case, only 25 mV under the 3.465 V GPIO/PMU maximum (RV1106 DS Table 3-2). TLV62569's VFB ±2 % is specified at TJ = 25 °C only (p.4), and ripple and load transients add on top. Luckfox's own 3.3 V rail runs at 0.8 × (1 + 40.2/13) ≈ 3.27 V.
fix: Use 45.3k/10.2k (3.265 V nominal, 3.15–3.39 V band) or 44.2k/10k (3.25 V). Update power_rails.csv and re-run P3.

issue: Two Luckfox attributions are wrong. power.md §2 says the U6 output capacitors are copied as '10 µF + 10 µF + 100 nF'; the Luckfox sheet shows C63 10 µF + C64 100 nF (+ C62 10 pF feed-forward). And R12 1K / C38 10nF are cited as the Luckfox 'Power Reset' block, but they sit next to the SoC in PART A. The 'Power Reset' block is Key1 + R22 100R + ED1 (not fitted). Whether to keep the Luckfox reset button Key1 is not decided anywhere.
fix: Correct both citations in power.md and D-34. Record in decisions.md whether Key1/R22 is kept as a reset button.

issue: power_rails.csv gives VCC3V3_SD (Q_SD SI2301) a 2.0 A rating marked UNVERIFIED, yet check P5 reports it as PASS. A gate clause should not pass on an uncited number.
fix: Cite the SI2301 datasheet's continuous drain current at 70 °C, or treat the rating like the USB-A switch: a Phase 4 requirement (≥ 0.26 A), marked as such and skipped by P5.

issue: The hard-off timing spread for C_PDT 0.82 µF X7R counts the ±10 % initial tolerance but not X7R's ±15 % change over temperature. With it, the worst-case hard-off point is 5257 ms × 1.174 × 1.10 × 1.15 + 82 + 41 ≈ 7.93 s. That is still under 8 s, but with only 70 ms to spare, and the datasheet spread is only given at 1500 pF (LTC2954 p.3).
fix: Add the temperature coefficient to P8, or drop C_PDT to 0.68 µF (nominal about 4.4 s, worst case about 6.7 s). This depends on the human's answer to open question Q1 about what '≥ 8 s' means.

issue: LCSC C683783 (LTC2954CTS8-2#TRPBF, TSOT-23-8) exists, but its page shows no stock or price. The whole R4 design depends on this one part. TLV62569DBVR (C141836) appears in stock at LCSC per web search; JLCPCB stock was not confirmed for either part.
fix: Phase 4 must confirm LTC2954 stock ≥ 100 at LCSC/JLCPCB. Otherwise switch to the D-03 F1/F2 fallback, and keep power.md §6 independent of the part where possible.

issue: Check P10 and the rail table count only the capacitors next to each regulator against TLV62569 Table 4 (p.9). The SoC decoupling on the same rails is ignored. The Luckfox sheet has C22–C28 on VDD_0V9 (10+10+1+1 µF + 3×100 nF = 22.3 µF) and C15–C17 on VDD_ARM (11.1 µF), and the two rails are joined through R32. With U4's local 2×22 µF the regulator loop sees about 77 µF. TI has tested only 2×22 µF at 0.6–1.2 V with 2.2 µH (its +20 % allowance reaches about 53 µF), and no 100 µF combination is tested in any row. The core-rail loop could ring or oscillate and stop the board from booting.
fix: Define a total output-capacitance budget for each rail: the capacitors next to the regulator plus all SoC and peripheral decoupling Phase 5 will place (Luckfox values). Make P10 and power_rails.csv use that total. For U4, either fit a 10 µF + 100 nF local capacitor with the Luckfox SoC-side set (total about 43 µF ≈ 2×22 µF), or keep 2×22 µF locally and limit the SoC-side capacitors on VDD_0V9/VDD_ARM to 1 µF/100 nF. Repeat for VCC_DDR (22 + 21.1 µF matches the tested 2×22 µF cell), VCC_1V8 and VCC_3V3, and record the decision in decisions.md.

issue: architecture.md §3 (around line 125) still says in bold 'Rev A rule: fit R41 = 1 kΩ from VCC5V0_SYS to PWR_EN'. This contradicts D-34/D-38 round 2, which feed R41 from VCC_1V8. If Phase 5 wires it from VCC5V0_SYS, the 3.3 V regulator can start before VCC_DDR is up (check P7b fails).
fix: Rewrite that architecture.md paragraph to say R41 1 kΩ is fed from VCC_1V8 and C65 is 150 nF (D-34 r2), and remove the 'Phase 3 alternative' sentence.

issue: The Luckfox sheet prints R32 (VDD_0V9 → VDD_ARM) as '0R 5% DNP'. power.md and D-06 describe it as a plain copy of a 0 Ω link. If a later phase copies the DNP marking, CPU_DVDD (pin 115) has no supply and the board cannot boot.
fix: In power.md §1/§2 and D-06, state that R32 0 Ω is FITTED (or replaced by a direct copper connection), as a deviation from the Luckfox DNP marking, and require Phase 4/5 to carry it as fitted.

issue: The Luckfox hand note '200K->100K' next to R14 suggests Luckfox builds with 100 kΩ. With 100 kΩ, check P7a fails: U5/U7 can enable at 0.71 ms, before U4 is good at 0.91 ms. The design keeps 200 kΩ but calls it simply the Luckfox value.

issue: Check P11 claims every restart repeats the cold-start order, but it only checks VCC5V0_SYS, C77 and C65. VCC_3V3 has 10 µF plus the SoC capacitors, no bleed resistor, and a power LED whose current falls off near its forward voltage. It can still be about 1.5–2 V at the earliest restart (226 ms) while VDD_0V9 is 0 V.
fix: Either add a 1 kΩ bleed resistor on VCC_3V3 (about 11 mW, add it to the budget) and extend P11 to all four rails, or reword §3/D-42 to say only the enable capacitors are guaranteed reset and note that some voltage may remain on VCC_3V3.

issue: §6.3 estimates the switch's turn-off stress from the turn-on gate current. At turn-off the enable output is open, so the gate discharges only through R_GS: 5–20 µA, giving a drain fall of 0.45–2.2 V/ms. Q_PWR can carry the falling load for up to about 6 ms, roughly 5–15 mJ rather than the stated 2–4 mJ.
fix: Recompute the turn-off time and energy using a gate current of |Vplateau| / R_GS, compare it with the AO3401A safe-operating-area curve, and update §6.3 and D-41.

issue: Check P8 scales the force-off timer spread from the LTC2954 timing spec at 1500 pF. The timer pin current is specified at ±20 % (2.4–3.6 µA, p.3), which for large capacitors gives a worst case of about 7.0 s rather than 6.6 s. That is still under 8 s, but the check does not cover it.
fix: Add the ±20 % timer-current corner to P8 and §6.2 (worst case about 7.0 s, still under 8 s).

issue: The VBUS_USBA row of the rail table says 'USB ≥ 4.75 V at port'. After the 0.26 V input drop and the USB-A switch, a 5.00 V charger gives about 4.69 V at the port, and a 4.75 V charger about 4.4 V.

issue: PLAN test point TP8 is defined as 'PWR_EN / button controller out', but in this design PWR_EN is now the U6 enable fed from VCC_1V8, and power.md puts TP8 on VCC5V0_SYS. The naming is ambiguous for Phase 6.

issue: Check P3 has a ripple/transient headroom rule only for VCC_3V3 (at least 50 mV below the maximum). VDD_0V9's set-point band 0.876–0.924 V leaves only 26 mV on each side of the shared 0.85–0.95 V window. VCC_DDR's 1.405 V top edge leaves 45 mV below the 1.45 V absolute maximum ([DS] Table 3-1/3-2 p.20). A mutation of the DDR top resistor to 130 kΩ (top edge 1.424 V) still passes P3. These rails can be overstressed by load-step overshoot.

In power.md §2, record a load-transient budget for VDD_0V9 and VCC_DDR (TLV62569 load-step plot, 10 µF local capacitor). Add 'TP4/TP5 under CPU/DDR load steps' to the Phase-6 measurements. Optionally, a 124 kΩ top resistor for VCC_DDR (1.303–1.386 V band) gives 64 mV of margin to 1.45 V.

issue: Two 0R 0603 parts (C21189: 1 A rated, up to 50 mΩ; UNI-ROYAL datasheet p.5 §7) sit in series with the CPU core supply. (1) The VDD_0V9 measurement link on the U4 output carries the full 1.001 A worst case from power_rails.csv: 100 % of its rating, so the 1.3× rule fails. (2) It is followed by R32 [R33], the VDD_0V9 to VDD_ARM link, carrying 0.5 A. The worst-case drop is 50 + 25 = 75 mV. check_power P3 treats the 0R link as 0 Ω and reports a VDD_ARM low edge of 0.876 V; including the links it falls to about 0.80 V, below the 0.85 V CPU_DVDD minimum in RV1106 datasheet r1.8 p.20 Table 3-2. A core rail this far below spec could make the first boot unstable at 1.2 GHz.

(a) Replace R32 [R33] with a direct copper connection or KiCad net-tie; power.md line 102 already allows 'replace it by a direct copper connection'. (b) Replace the U4 output measurement link with a normally-closed solder jumper (a copper bridge cut to measure), or require Phase 5 to tap the U4 feedback divider top (R17) after the link. Then the qty-5 C21189 line in make_bom.py drops to 3 links plus whatever stays fitted; no new part type and about $0 cost change. (c) Add a P3 term in check_power.py: for every 0R link, subtract 0.05 Ω × the link's worst-case current from the band low edge, and check link current ≤ rating / 1.3. If a fitted part is still wanted on VDD_0V9, an 0805 0R (C17477, Basic, 6.17 M stock, 2 A rated per the same datasheet p.5) fixes the rating but not the drop, so it must be paired with feedback sensing after the link. Record the change as a decision and re-run check_power and check_bom.

issue: At the CPU (VDD_ARM), the worst-case DC low edge is 0.873 V against the 0.85 V CPU_DVDD minimum, a margin of 23 mV. That figure comes from check_power P3L and RV1106 datasheet r1.8 p.20 Table 3-2. Nothing budgets regulator ripple, load-step droop, or the copper and via drop from U4 to pin 115 against those 23 mV: power.md and D-68 only say 'PCB trace drop U4->SoC is a Phase 7 rule', without a number. Phase 7 could use up the margin without anyone noticing.
fix:
Put a numeric allowance into power.md §2 and D-68, and add it to the P3L check in check_power.py so the check fails if the allowance is exceeded. An example allowance:
- U4-to-pin-115 copper and vias: 8 mV or less at 1.0 A.
- Ripple plus load transient: 15 mV or less.

Alternatively, raise the U4 feedback top resistor from 49.9k to 51.1k. That gives a band of about 0.883 to 0.931 V, still inside the 0.81 to 0.95 V logic range. A Basic 51.1k 0603 part is UNVERIFIED and would need confirming first. Re-run check_power afterwards.

issue: The TF-01A socket's card-detect behaviour is UNVERIFIED. Luckfox's socket has a separate two-terminal switch (CD1 pin 9 to GND, CD2 pin 10 to R54 to SDMMC_DET). Our TF-01A has a single 'cd' contact (pin 9) that only works if it closes to the grounded shell when a card is inserted. If it does not, Linux never sees the card, so a root filesystem on SD would not mount during bring-up.
fix: Phase 7: when drawing board:microSD_TF-01A, confirm from the TF-01A drawing or LCSC page which side the cd contact switches against. Phase 8: write in the DTS notes a ready fallback for the sdmmc node (`broken-cd;` card polling, or `cd-inverted`) so a wrong polarity is a software fix. Phase 6 bringup.md: measure SDMMC_DET with and without a card before the first SD boot.

issue:
bringup.md Step 2 (the first time power is applied) runs with JP1 bridged and R29, R30 and R31 fitted. Step 3 'Prepare' does the isolation only afterwards. Step 2 can fail because:
- the gate network lets Q_PWR conduct at plug-in;
- Q_PWR has a D-S short;
- the wrong SOT-23 reel is fitted. AO3400A is also in this BOM (Q3). Fitted as Q1, its body diode passes VBUS_5V to VCC5V0_SYS at plug-in.

If that happens, VCC5V0_SYS rises without a button press and the regulators start:
- U4 EN is pulled up from VCC5V0_SYS (R23).
- U5 and U7 start through R20/C20.
- U6 follows from VCC_1V8.

Their outputs reach the SoC before any of them has been measured. Step 1 cannot detect a swapped divider (bringup.md says so itself). Such a divider puts 1.8 V on a core rail with a 0.99 V abs-max (RV1106 datasheet r1.8 Table 3-1 p.20). So the procedure does not meet its own D-78 claim, or the gate clause, that a failure at one step cannot damage the board at the next step.

Several unpowered resistance expectations ignore body-diode paths through the regulators and switches:
- Step 3.1 expects JP1 pad 1 to pad 2 = 140–160 kΩ. In either polarity, a path also runs from pad 1 through L1, the U4 SW body diodes and VIN to R_BL5 (470 Ω) and GND, so a DMM will read far below 140 kΩ. That would look like a failed check.
- Step 1 expects TP16 to GND ≈ 10 kΩ. With red on TP16, the Q4 body diode conducts into VCC_3V3 and R_BL33 (680 Ω), so it reads lower.
- The 'every pair ≈ sum of the two to-GND readings' claim fails for the same reason.
fix:
State the lead polarity (black on TP19). Then:
- JP1 check: accept 'not ≈ 0 Ω, continuity beeper silent / > 1 kΩ'.
- TP16: accept > 500 Ω.
- Rail pairs: accept > 100 Ω and add the note 'diode paths make these readings polarity dependent'.
- Keep the 'compare with board #2 within 10 %' rule.

issue: Step 3 uses a 100 mA current limit. Turn-on inrush into VCC5V0_SYS is up to 0.65 A (60.5 µF, power.md §6.3 and check P9), and VBUS_5V has only about 2.8 µF (C2, C3, C4). A supply with a fast constant-current loop can let VBUS_5V sag below the LTC2954 undervoltage lockout (2.2–2.5 V, LTC2954 datasheet p.3). The board would then switch on and off at once, giving a false stop at the most important step. No damage, but it is confusing.
fix: Add a note to Steps 3 and 4: put a ≥ 470 µF electrolytic across VBUS/GND at the USB-C breakout. If the board switches on and immediately off at 100 mA, re-check the Step-1 readings and retry at 300 mA. Record which limit was used.

issue: In step 3, with JP_MEAS_0V9 [JP1] cut, U4 drives only C_OUT_U4 [C24] 10 uF + C16 100 nF. TLV62569 Table 4 (SLVSDG1C p.9) has only one checked combination for 0.6–1.2 V with 2.2 uH: 2x22 uF. D-47 meets that only with the SoC-side capacitors connected. So isolated U4 runs with an output filter that is not proven stable, and the step-3 reading on JP1 pad 1 checks only the DC set-point. A marginal loop can give an unstable reading or one above 0.94 V on a good board (false stop). Nothing is damaged, because the output is isolated. U5/U6/U7 in the isolated state are in checked cells (22 / 10 / 22 uF).

Add an optional fix for an unstable or high reading: clip a temporary 22 uF or larger ceramic, rated 6.3 V or more, from JP1 pad 1 to TP19, then re-measure.

issue: testpoints.md TP27 (PB_INT_N) gives 'idle >= 2.55 V', and bringup.md step 5.3 says 'TP27 ≈ TP2'. issue: Several placement zones in layout/zones.csv and placement.csv hold more KiCad courtyard area than the zone itself. Areas come from the cached footprints in refs/kicad-footprints-*; zone area does not count routing space. (1) Z-SOC (27–43, 25–41 = 256 mm²): 67 parts. U9 alone is about 13.5 × 13.5 = 182 mm², and the other 66 parts (23 × 100 nF, 7 × 1 µF, 6 × 10 µF 0603, 2 × 4.7 µF, 3 ferrite beads, SOD-123, net tie, 6 test pads, resistors) add about 146 mm². Total about 328 mm², or 128 % of the zone. In §5.3/§6.1 the pad toes sit at 6.45 mm from the SoC centre and the first escape via at ≥ 7.45 mm, so the 'ring just outside the escape region' is only 0.55 mm wide before the zone edge at 8.0 mm. The neighbouring zones (Z-ETH x ≤ 27, Z-XTAL1 y ≤ 25, Z-NAND x ≥ 44.5, Z-XTAL2/Z-SDPWR/Z-USB y ≥ 41–44) leave it no room to grow. (2) Z-PWRIN (197 mm²): about 200 mm² of courtyards (SMA, 1812, SW1 TS-1187A, U1, U3, Q1–Q3, passives) plus about 10 test pads, i.e. over 100 %. (3) Z-NAND is 97 % full (the WSON-8 8 × 6 courtyard is 8.7 × 6.5 in a 9.3 × 8 zone). (4) Z-USBA-PWR is 87 % full (the C35 6.3 mm polymer cap alone is 9.6 × 7.1). check_layout L6 only tests rectangle overlap and edge contact, so it passes a floor plan that cannot be placed. The length rules derived from it (ETH ≤ 30 mm, FSPI ≤ 25 mm, decoupler ≤ 3 mm) will also break when H1 has to rearrange the floor plan.
fix: Re-plan the zones in tools/layout_calc.py and regenerate. (a) Make Z-SOC at least about 22 × 22 mm (±11 mm from (35, 33)). Move Z-XTAL1, Z-ETH, Z-NAND, Z-XTAL2, Z-USB and Z-SDPWR outward, using the spare area in Z-PMU (47 % full), Z-ETH (16 %) and Z-SDPWR (26 %). (b) Relax §5.3 by value: 100 nF caps ≤ 3 mm of trace from their pin; 1 µF / 4.7 µF / 10 µF caps, ferrite beads and sub-rail test pads TP18/TP22–TP26 ≤ 8 mm, placed outside the first ring. (c) Make Z-PWRIN, Z-NAND and Z-USBA-PWR at least 2 × their courtyard sum, e.g. Z-PWRIN about 400 mm², using the room south of Z-PMU. (d) Add a capacity test to check_layout L6: the sum of cached KiCad courtyard areas per zone must be ≤ 55 % of the zone area. Also check that the whole-board courtyard total, now about 53 % of 70 × 70 before routing, still fits. If it does not fit at ≤ 55 % per zone, enlarge the board under the D-H2 'larger if it makes the build simpler' allowance (e.g. 80 × 70) and record the cost change. Record the change in decisions.md as an update to D-84.

issue: layout/board.kicad_dru will report errors that the checklist ('KiCad DRC: 0 errors') cannot clear without editing the rules. (a) The 'ETH/USB pairs keep 30 mil from other nets' rules apply to pads too. ETH_RXN pin 97 sits next to pin 96 (ETH_AVDD1V8) and TXP 100 next to 101 (FEPHY_AVDD3V3) with a 0.16 mm gap. USB DM 26 / DP 27 sit next to pins 25 and 28. On J1, A5↔A6 and B5↔B6 have a 0.7 mm gap and A8↔B6 0.2 mm. U11 has a 0.5 mm pitch, and the U1/U2 SOT-23-6 pins are 0.95 mm apart. All of these break the 0.76 mm rule. The later 'escape neck-down' rule only covers A.Type == 'track' inside U9. (b) `(constraint skew (max 1.27mm))` without `within_diff_pairs` compares all 8 ETH_DIFF nets with each other, including the short _J segments after R56–R59, and all 6 USB_DIFF nets, so it gives false skew errors. KiCad also does not add length through the 0 Ω links, R47 or R48, so those totals must be summed by hand. (c) `A.Type != 'NPTH'` is not a valid KiCad type value.
fix: Restrict the 0.76 mm rules to tracks outside the fine-pitch parts. Example: `(condition "A.NetClass == 'ETH_DIFF' && A.Type == 'track' && B.Type == 'track' && B.NetClass != 'ETH_DIFF' && B.NetClass != 'GND' && !A.intersectsCourtyard('U9')")`, and the same for USB with !A.intersectsCourtyard('J1'/'U1'/'U2'/'U11'). Use `(constraint skew (max 1.27mm) (within_diff_pairs))`. Replace the edge rule's condition with a plain global edge_clearance of 0.4 mm. In §10, note that ETH and SDMMC/FSPI clock lengths across R56–R59, R47 and R48 are summed by hand.

issue: Z-PMU (x 62–79.4) and Z-PWRIN (x 55–79.4) run to 0.6 mm from the east V-cut at x = 80. Add a §5 and §10 rule: no MLCC within 3 mm of x = 0 or x = 80, and MLCCs within 5 mm of a V-cut must lie parallel to it. Note in §8 that the rails should be broken off with a depaneling tool or pliers, not by bending the board.

issue: vdd_arm is a regulator-fixed with regulator-min-microvolt 800000 and regulator-max-microvolt 1000000. This is copied from Luckfox ipc.dtsi L43-51. The SDK drivers/regulator/fixed.c (L106-112, fetched from the LuckfoxTECH/luckfox-pico main branch into design/refs/verifier-p8-src-2026-10-29/) rejects a fixed regulator whose min and max differ: "Fixed regulator specified with variable voltages", -EINVAL. cpu-supply then never resolves, so cpufreq most likely stays deferred. The CPU then runs at the ARMCLK the CRU sets at boot, 1104 MHz (rv1106.dtsi L704-717). The board still boots. (b) Set regulator-min-microvolt and regulator-max-microvolt both to <900000> in rv1106-custom-reva.dtsi so cpufreq works with the 1.2 GHz cap; this is a deviation from Luckfox and needs a bring-up check. issue: /etc/default/board ships with USB_MODE=auto. In the default host DTS, S15board therefore sets USB_SEL high and switches USB-A VBUS on at the first Linux boot (bring-up step 8). That happens before the scoped, monitored first enable in bring-up step 11.1. README §7 only says to set USB_MODE=off "before that step", which is too late. It cannot damage the board: the SY6280 limits current and nothing is plugged in. But it breaks the step-ordering intent of gate TP-D6, and the TP13 dip during step 8 goes unobserved.

issue: README §10.1 and bringup.md step 9.1 say the console shows 'POWER button pressed: clean shutdown'. But /etc/acpi/PWRF/00000080 writes that line with `logger`, which goes to syslog. acpid also redirects its children's output to /var/log/acpid.log. Only init's shutdown messages reach the console, so a bench user may think the button did nothing.

- C74 (pin 71) sits 3.3 mm west, across pins 72–80 (9 header/UART signals).
- C55 and C60 (pin 70) sit 1.5 and 2.5 mm west.
- C62 (81) is 0.8 mm off; C50 (103) is 1.8 mm off, across header pins 104–107; C68 (108) is 1.1 mm off.
- C61 (61) and R46 (58) are about 0.75 mm off.

North side: 14 signal pins (72–80, 83–87) plus VDD_0V9 pin 82 lie in t −2.3…+2.9 mm, with only 8 single-trace exits. West side: header pins 109–114 have 2 exits. placement-review.md says these signals 'pass between ring-1 parts or use vias, as §6.1 expects', but my own channel analysis (scratchpad/escape.py) does not bear this out.

Re-place ring 1 in place.py:
(a) Put each 100 nF directly in front of its own supply pin, sideways offset ≤ 0.5 mm.
(b) Move the row out so the via ring at r ≥ 7.45 mm stays free: inner cap pad edge ≥ about 7.9 mm from the U9 centre, i.e. the row about 2.6 mm outside the pad line. The ≤ 3 mm rule still holds (about 1.8 mm edge distance).
(c) Leave contiguous channels in front of each group of signal pins, sized at about 0.3 mm per DEFAULT trace and 0.35 mm per SDMMC/FSPI trace. For example, about 3 mm in front of pins 72–80, about 1.6 mm for 83–87 and about 2 mm for 109–114.
(d) If header GPIOs are meant to drop to L4 through vias in the inner ring (between the pad heels and the EP), record that as a D-number deviation from layout.md §6.1.

issue: The FSPI fan-out on the U9 east side needs a crossing on L1, and layout.md §2.3 forbids FSPI on L4. C53's pad sits directly in front of pin 48, and C63 (pin 43, VCC_3V3) sits in the middle of the bus (t 1.97–2.59). So the 48→R47 link cuts across the exit of pin 47. Pins 47 and 44 also have only the 0.43 mm gaps C53–R47 and R47–C63 to leave through: 1 trace each at neck-down, 0 at the FSPI 0.15/0.20 class rule. They cannot pass C63's radial link to pin 43.

Move C63 out of the FSPI fan, for example south of pin 39 in the open area at t > 3.4, or tangentially at the SE corner. This keeps pins 39–48 a contiguous FSPI channel at least 2.4 mm wide (6 traces at 0.15/0.20) in front of the pins.

issue: FSPI needs two crossings whatever the placement. issue: The USB pairs cannot be routed on L1 without crossovers. (1) The SoC has pin 26 DM west and pin 27 DP east, but U11 has pin 8 DP west and pin 7 DM east. P/N is reversed, so 'the USB pair goes straight from pins 26/27 to U11' is impossible. (2) The U11 USB-A pair (pins 3 DP, 4 DM, west to east) arrives at U2 and J4 (DM west, DP east) reversed. (3) The USB-C pair (U11 pins 1/2, west) must go south-east to J1 while the USB-A pair (pins 3/4, east) goes south-west, so the pairs must cross. With the SoC north, J4 south-west and J1 south-east there is no U11 position or rotation on the board that avoids this. layout.md allows at most 4 vias per line but §2.3 forbids USB_DIFF on L4.

Combine them with the unavoidable USB-C A6/B6–A7/B7 join crossover where possible. Record a D-number deviation from §2.3 (USB_DIFF briefly on L4) for owner approval. Move or rotate U11, U2 and U1 if that removes a swap, and correct the placement-review.md text.

The only via-free path, coming in from the north under the J3 body past the SH pads, has a 1.3 mm SH-to-pin-1 gap and is likely over 30 mm. issue: As routed, the TX pair is uncoupled for 11.89 mm (P line), against the 6.7 mm shown when D-108 b was approved at D-H5. The DRU limit was raised to 14 mm in L4 (D-111). issue: The 'hop' class of the impedance check counts every point within 1.5 mm of a pair via as controlled. issue: The executor hands USB_SEL, PB_INT_N and SDMMC_PWREN to the owner, but the fix needs no placement or schematic change: it is a rerouting of the two L4 SENSE tracks (RECOVERY, SARADC_IN1). For SDMMC_PWREN, `l5_inner_probe` only sampled via sites south of the pocket (x 41.55-42.25, y 36.5-42.5). It never tried the north-east: between RECOVERY's corner (44.91, 27.38) and the VCC_1V8 L4 end (44.923, 28.347) there is about 0.74 mm of copper gap. That is enough for a 0.10 or 0.15 mm track with 0.25/0.20 mm clearances. Also covers blocks sd, usb and pmu.

Then route USB_SEL, PB_INT_N and SDMMC_PWREN out on L4. Before that, also try the north-east exit for SDMMC_PWREN through the gap at (44.9, 27.4-28.35). Record the change as a new D-number, re-run the L4 checks (SENSE clearance at least 2 mm from SW nodes and inductors, 0 FAIL) and the gate.
